title: 📌Kaipara harbour coastal
description:
***Join us on Sunday, October 4th for the Kaipara Coast to Shelly Beach Hike as we explore the shores of the Kaipara Harbour—the largest natural harbour in the Southern Hemisphere! Starting at South Head, we will make our way south along the coastline to Shelly Beach, taking in vast tidal flats, coastal farmland, sand beaches, and mangroves along the way. While no swimming is required, you can expect wading and some muddy patches, so come prepared to get partially wet. Please note that this hike requires a car shuttle, and details are in this description.***
📌 New members are welcome
📌 If you find yourself on the "waiting list" and decide to attend the hike on the day of the event, then please be aware that you will need to hike separately from the group. Only those listed as "Going" are considered valid participants.
There are no "plus ones"- If you want to go, then you will need to register with meetup
📌 Individuals who are unfit or prefer a slower pace are kindly requested not to RSVP. Slow people will hold up the group, as everyone will have to wait for you to catch up. There are alternative Meetup groups available for those who enjoy walking very slowly.
📌If you are unable to attend, please update your status to avoid a "No Show" being recorded next to your name. Accumulating three or more "No Shows" will result in your status being changed to "Not going." It is always polite to adjust your RSVP status if you can no longer participate. Thank you👍

🚩Summary of Main Details:
📌 Meet: Wellington St Convenience store (unless a direct driver)
📌 Hike Duration: Approx 6.5 hours including breaks (estimated)
📌 Distance: About 20km
📌 Map of hike: https://tinyurl.com/3af794v4
📌 Difficulty: 3.0 on our 1-5 scale.
📌 Speed: medium to fast pace
📌 Toilets: None - find some bushes.

🚩 Time Guideline :
07:30 Good time to arrive at Wellington street
07:45 Arrange car pooling
07:50 Leave Wellington Street
08:40 Direct drivers arrive at Shelly Beach Road

title: Build Night: Demos, Collabs & Open Source in Practice
description:
A fortnightly, hands-on session focused on the projects the Auckland AI Collective is actually building — together.

Each session centres on **demonstrations** of what members are working on. Expect live demos, group experiments, and the occasional "let's just try it and see what happens" moment — so come ready to get involved, not just watch. Some parts may invite your participation; none of it is polished or precious.

The tone is **casual and informal**\- eat dinner\, drink\, and enjoy\. This is a place to share ideas\, get feedback\, find collaborators\, and turn "someone should build that" into an actual repo\.

What we cover will vary week to week depending on what people bring and what the group is curious about — the constant is the room: builders comparing notes and starting things together.

**This is for you if** you want to get directly and personally involved in group projects, collaborations, and **open source**.

See what we're already building on GitHub: [https://github.com/auckland-ai-collective](https://github.com/auckland-ai-collective)

Bring a project, a problem, an idea, or just yourself.

After this session we can hang out as long as we like at the restaurant if you want to keep the conversation going and connect with other professionals.

title: Building an AI Language App with Flutter
description:
Looking for a chill but productive space to code, learn, and connect with other developers? Whether you’re just starting out or deep into a side project, you’re welcome here.

🚨 **Special Feature This Week: Building a Multi-Platform AI App**

This week features a deep dive by [Ethan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/huanglisen/), who will be walking us through exactly how he built Bantera ([https://bantera.app/](https://bantera.app/)), an English speaking and listening app.
He’ll be breaking down his stack and process:

* **The Cross-Platform Build:** How he engineered the backend and deployed the application across the web, iOS, and Android using Flutter.
* **The AI Integration:** His approach to wiring generative AI directly into the system to automatically output text, images, and audio.
* **The Product Design:** How he brought all the pieces together into a cohesive language-learning experience.

Alongside the demo, this remains a casual, community-driven space where you can:

* 💻 Work on your own coding projects
* 🎯 Share goals or progress (totally optional!)
* 🎙️ Talk tech, app development, and AI integration
* ☕ Meet like-minded people over coffee

Come with your laptop, your curiosity, or just a love for tech. Stay for the connections and good vibes.

☕ This event is hosted at a local café, so we kindly ask that you support the venue by purchasing a drink or snack if you can.
No pressure, no strict schedule—just code, coffee, AI, and vibes.
We usually hold meetups every fortnight (bi-weekly)—use them to connect, share, and learn from others.

For your deep work sessions between meetups, feel free to try NeonContext: a Voice AI tool designed to help you stay focused and hit your flow state. This is a tool developed within our community, so feel free to check it out and share your feedback! 💬 [https://www.neoncontext.com/](https://www.neoncontext.com/)

title: From Vibe Coding to Production AI on AWS
location: Level 19, Vero Centre, 48 Shortland Street, Auckland CBD, Auckland
description:
Hello everyone,

Welcome to the September edition of the Auckland AWS Tools & Programming Meetup! This month, we are diving deep into the lifecycle of building and scaling AI-powered products—from a single idea and "vibe coding" all the way to robust engineering practices for production systems on AWS.

🚨 **Action Required:** To help us streamline building security and sort out the catering (including dietary requirements), please make sure to pre-register before arriving: 👉 **[Pre-register for Venue Check-In Here](https://eventspaces.app/e/auckland-aws-tools-and-programming-meetup-sept-24-from-vibe-coding-to-production-ai-on-aws-a9b5de/register)**

Join us for an exciting double-header exploring the realities of shipping real software:

**Speaker 1: Dinesh Sharma**
**From Zero to Qazo: Building a Product with Kiro, AI & AWS**

**About the Talk:** "I started Qazo with a simple idea and used Kiro and AI to turn it into a real product, eventually deploying it on AWS. This session is about that journey — what worked, what didn't, the lessons I learned from vibe coding, and why I think everyone should try building something of their own to experience the full journey from idea → build → break → learn → deploy."
🔗 **Check out Qazo:** [https://qazo.net](https://qazo.net)

**Speaker 2: Dinesh Liyanage**

**After the Demo: From Vibe Coding to AI Engineering**
**About the Talk:** "I pick up from where Dinesh's session ends. Vibe coding gets you to a working product, and that's genuinely new, but a demo and a product with paying customers are different animals. I'll go through what breaks on the way between them and the engineering practices that fix it:

* **Evals** so prompt changes stop being guesswork.
* **Tracing** so you can reproduce the bad output a customer reported.
* **Cost and model routing** so unit economics survive growth.
* **Context engineering** so quality doesn't quietly rot as you add data.
